participants.note: Concept ACK; suggested CheckArgFlags simplification, test restructuring, and questioned runtime checking
moved PR to draft because base PR is a draft

claims.harm: CheckArgFlags needlessly allows ALLOW_ANY types to be included in forbid logic
claims.quote: I don't think it makes sense to ever include any of the `ALLOW_ANY` types in `forbid`

claims.harm: special helper functions tweaking flags clutter the tests compared to structured table-driven testing
claims.quote: I think it might be better to restructure the tests than have these special functions that tweak the flags.
claims.settled_by_quote: I'm not too inclined to want to restructure the tests, though I'd be happy to review a PR that did.

claims.harm: argument flags are enforced via runtime assertions rather than compile-time checks
claims.quote: shame all these checks are happening at runtime rather than compile time though
claims.settled_by_quote: Switching enforcement from runtime to compile time after constraints are in already place would be easier by comparison

support.reason: Concept ACK, shame all these checks are happening at runtime rather than compile time though

result.notes: Initial record. hebasto, promag, and ajtowns gave Concept ACKs. ajtowns suggested simplifying CheckArgFlags, restructuring unit tests, and noted compile-time checks would be preferable; ryanofsky simplified the check, explained his reasoning for the test and runtime approach, and no further objections were raised.
